description: A module's top level IS the configuration namespace, in the framework that has no configuration object. The secret rules match a write into something -- `app.config["SECRET_KEY"]`, `app.secret_key` -- because Flask gives them an object; Django gives them none, since `django.conf.settings.SECRET_KEY` reads the module-level name of whichever module the deployment points at. The write has no base and no property, so one of the two largest Python web frameworks had no hardcoded-secret rule that applied to it, and doccano's committed fallback key recorded nothing. The value half is the other spelling of `X || literal`: every library says default with an ARGUMENT rather than an operator, and the argument after the key is the one that means it. Three positives cover the three spellings -- environs' callable, `os.environ.get`, and the `default=` keyword. Five negatives, and the first two are the near misses that decide the rule. `env("REAL_SECRET_KEY")` with no fallback is the CORRECT way to write the line and its key is credential-shaped exactly as the fallbacks are, so admitting the first argument would report the fix the finding recommends; and `graphene.String(description="Password.")` in a class body is saleor's measured case twice over -- a class body is reached from the module's top level and is not part of it, and a keyword that accompanies a value is not one that names a default. The rest are a value incapable of serving as the credential, a key with no credential word, and a CSRF token, which are the same three bars the property-write rule applies. A module-level setting assigned a PLAIN literal is a stated miss, recorded in the model beside the rule: the literal analysis already judges those by shape, and widening this one to claim them reported two lines in this engine's own corpus that no expectation names.

expected.note: doccano's line: the fallback becomes the signing key whenever the deployment supplies nothing, which is what its own image and documented run command both do
the stdlib spelling of the same shape
the keyword spelling, which is what python-decouple and environs both write
